name: VARA Rulebooks — Virtual Asset Service Provider Licensing (Dubai)

articles.title: Scope — Dubai (excluding DIFC)
articles.requirement: Captures Virtual Asset Service Providers operating in Dubai, excluding DIFC (which is supervised by DFSA). Activities covered by VARA: advisory, broker-dealer, custody, exchange, lending + borrowing, management + investment, transfer + settlement. Cross-VARA-with-onshore-UAE activities subject to additional federal supervision (CBUAE / SCA) where applicable.

articles.title: Category 1 — Advisory services
articles.requirement: Provision of advice on virtual assets, including investment recommendations, portfolio composition, transactions. Capital, fit-and-proper, conduct + market-conduct, conflicts-of-interest rules. AML/CFT alignment with FDL 10/2025 mandatory. Notification + record-keeping requirements.

articles.title: Category 2 — Broker-Dealer services
articles.requirement: Buying / selling virtual assets for own account or on behalf of customers; market-making. Substantial capital + segregation-of-customer-asset requirements. Best-execution standard. AML/CFT alignment with FDL 10/2025 + custody alignment with the VARA Custody Services Rulebook.

articles.title: Category 3 — Custody services
articles.requirement: Holding + safekeeping of virtual assets on behalf of customers. Customer-asset segregation (insolvency-remote); cold + hot wallet architecture proportionate to risk; key-management (MPC, HSM, multi-sig — proportionate to scale); independent assurance; reporting of customer balances. The most-scrutinised category given the bearer-instrument nature of virtual assets.

articles.title: Category 4 — Exchange services
articles.requirement: Operating an exchange platform for virtual assets (matching buyers + sellers; price discovery; trade execution). Market-conduct rules (anti-manipulation, fair-pricing, surveillance), KYC + AML alignment, listing standards, customer asset-safeguarding, technology resilience. Large operational + governance footprint.

articles.title: Category 5 — Lending + Borrowing services
articles.requirement: Facilitating lending or borrowing of virtual assets. Counterparty-risk + collateral-management standards; disclosure to customers of the risk of loss; mandatory liquidation procedures; conflicts-of-interest controls. Tightened post-Celsius / Voyager / FTX collapses.

articles.title: Category 6 — Management + Investment services
articles.requirement: Discretionary investment management of virtual-asset portfolios; collective investment scheme management. Suitability + appropriateness assessment; conflicts-of-interest; client-asset segregation; performance reporting; redemption / withdrawal procedures.

articles.title: Category 7 — Transfer + Settlement services
articles.requirement: Facilitating transfer or settlement of virtual assets. AML / Travel Rule alignment (FATF R.16); transaction-monitoring; cybersecurity around transfer infrastructure; customer-asset protection. Captures cross-border transfer services.

articles.title: Compliance Rulebook (cross-cutting)
articles.requirement: Cross-cutting AML / market conduct / governance / risk management / technology / customer-asset-protection / disclosure rules applying to all licensed activities. Specific obligations: institution-wide risk assessment (incl. PF); CDD + EDD aligned with FDL 10/2025; SAR via goAML; sanctions screening; market-conduct rules + manipulation prevention; technology + cybersecurity standards; customer-asset segregation.

articles.title: Prohibited virtual assets + activities
articles.requirement: VARA prohibits: privacy tokens (Monero, Zcash, similar — anonymity-enhancing); algorithmic stablecoins (post-Terra collapse); anonymity-enhancing mixers / tumblers; specific high-risk DeFi structures lacking accountable parties. Quarterly review + supplement; aligned with ADGM FSRA prohibitions but distinct legal authority. Existing licensees with these exposures had transition windows to exit.

articles.title: Supervision + enforcement
articles.requirement: VARA supervisory powers: licence suspension or revocation; CMPs (substantial — multi-AED-millions for serious failings); prohibition orders against individuals; remediation orders; public censure. Active enforcement track record since 2023; coordinated with CBUAE + EOCN + Federal Public Prosecution for cross-jurisdictional cases. Licensees + applicants subject to ongoing supervisory engagement + on-site inspections.
